source: Defines probability on a sigma-algebra; states normalization, complement, and countable additivity; explains the measure analogy.
evidence: Transcript 60-421 s; book lines 3-21. The book retains each axiom and the weights/tiles explanation.

source: Introduces set difference A\B=A∩B^c with a Venn-diagram explanation.
States/proves P(∅)=0, the split identity P(B)=P(A∩B)+P(A^c∩B), monotonicity, and the two-set union formula.
evidence: Transcript 600-1501 s; book lines 31-71. The book supplies explicit proofs matching the spoken partitions.

source: Uses A⊆B and the split identity to obtain P(A)≤P(B).
For decreasing A_j with empty intersection, decomposes A_j into disjoint rings and identifies P(A_j) as a convergent-series tail tending to zero.
evidence: Transcript 1440-1921 s; book lines 73-85. A transcript phrase around 1620 s is formula-OCR garbling; the surrounding spoken decomposition and book formula agree.

source: Explains subadditivity by C_1=A_1 and C_n=A_n\(∪_{i<n}A_i), with C_n⊆A_n and unchanged union.
Defines binary and finite discrete probability, gives P(A)=Σ_{i∈A}p_i, checks bounds/complement, and assigns finite additivity as an exercise.
evidence: Transcript 2280-2821 s; book lines 98-116 and 230-237. Book adds a clear binary prototype at lines 101-102 and retains the assigned verification as exercise 1.

source: Defines finite uniform probability, applies it to 6/49, and distinguishes fixed win probability from reduced prize-sharing when avoiding date-like selections.
evidence: Transcript 3660-4201 s; book lines 117-127. Book accurately compresses the longer roulette/toto discussion.

source: Shows a uniform N-outcome experiment can be reduced to odd/even and asks for the odd probability when N is odd.
evidence: Transcript 4200-4440 s; book retains the requested odd-N exercise at lines 238-239; the optional model-reduction exposition is omitted.

source: Defines countable discrete masses, says no uniform distribution exists on a countably infinite set, and gives zeta(2) and geometric-distribution examples with a machine-versus-human memorylessness caveat.
Defines geometric probability by volume ratio on a finite-volume region; contrasts volume with cardinality; says a fixed point has probability zero; outlines Monte Carlo estimation.
evidence: Transcript 5160-5761 s; book lines 152-190. At 5400-5461 s the source expressly says not every subset of Ω is measurable and a concrete sigma-algebra is required, whereas book lines 159-160 say 'for every subset A⊆Ω'.

source: Names (Ω, A, P) a probability space and gives the finite uniform power-set example; stresses the term is not developed further.
Introduces conditioning after observing A with P(A)>0, gives P(B|A)=P(A∩B)/P(A), describes restriction/renormalization, and gives its geometric-area version.
